headline: In-line PCE and an AI selloff pull yields lower; franc and pound lead, dollar slips
summary: The dollar index eased about 0.15% to near 102.0 as September PCE matched forecasts, Q3 GDP's 3.4% beat was shrugged off, and Alphabet's record 12% plunge sent money into Treasuries, cutting the 10-year yield about 8bp to near 4.96%. The franc (+0.45%) and pound (+0.4%) led and the euro recovered from a five-month low after the ECB, while the Aussie (−0.35%) and Taiwan dollar lagged on the tech selloff.
drivers: Headline PCE rose 0.5% m/m (3.6% y/y) and core 0.3% (3.1%), both in line, while Q3 GDP grew 3.4% against 3.2% expected. With a December hike already priced, the dollar got no lift; December odds slipped to roughly 76–83% from about 85% and the 10-year yield fell about 8bp.
AI jitters: havens up, tech-linked FX down

Alphabet's record 12% fall on negative free cash flow dragged the Nasdaq down 1.38%, lifting the franc to 0.8244 and bonds. Foreigners sold about NT$68.8 billion of Taiwan stocks, pushing the Taiwan dollar 7.4 cents weaker to 32.492, and the Aussie fell back from 0.7068.
ECB holds, flags December; Lagarde to leave early

The ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.50% but said a December hike is firmly in play, and Lagarde will step down on Feb 7. The euro bounced from 1.1105, its lowest since May, to about 1.1180, as record shorts (about $19 billion) were trimmed.
view: Neutral with a mild softening bias over the next 1–2 weeks: hot PCE and strong growth failed to lift it because a December hike is priced, and AI-led bond buying is pulling yields down. I fade the dollar against the loonie, yen and ringgit, where central banks are hiking or leaning hawkish, but still back it against the euro and rupiah. A DXY close above 102.80 would make me dollar-positive; below 101.70 I would turn outright bearish.
ideas: Short from 157.50–157.80 (filled) as the BoJ signals December and Tokyo guards 160; for 155.00, stop 158.60.
Short from 1.4030–1.4050 (about 0.4% in favour) on BoC–Fed convergence; for 1.3850, stop 1.4080.
New: sell 4.065–4.075 before Bank Negara's Nov 5 meeting; for 4.020, stop 4.095.
review: USD/CAD's short holds about 0.4% in favour and USD/PHP's long from 63.50 about 0.55%, which I book as the peso firms on Manila's pledge to defend it; USD/IDR's long is about 0.75% up. EUR/USD, AUD/USD, USD/JPY and USD/KRW entries filled and sit near flat; USD/TWD's fade survived a test of 32.60 and EUR/JPY is about 0.1% against. USD/CNH's entry was missed again, so I lower it; ranges held, and the ringgit's break of 4.06 turns that range into a short.

eurusd.note: Up about 0.25% to 1.1180 after the ECB hold, from 1.1105, its lowest since May; ECB fixing 1.1130.
eurusd.why: Both sides moved. The euro fell to 1.1105 before the ECB, then recovered as the bank held at 2.50% but said a December hike is firmly in play, and investors trimmed a decade-high short of about $19 billion. Lower US yields after in-line PCE and the tech selloff then softened the dollar. Lagarde's early exit on Feb 7 was expected and barely moved it.
eurusd.outlook: Still bearish but less one-way: I hold the short from 1.1170–1.1190 for 1.1050, as French spreads and $115 oil weigh. A close above 1.1240, likely on a hot euro-area CPI that cements a December ECB hike, ends the call.
eurusd.watch: Euro-area flash CPI (Oct 30), French spreads and US payrolls in early November.

gbpusd.note: Up 0.4% to 1.3378, the highest 5pm close since Oct 22, as the euro fell against sterling.
gbpusd.why: Sterling did some of the moving. With a BoE hike on Nov 5 fully priced and a second by February, the pound is October's best major, and EUR/GBP slipped to about 0.835. The rest came from a softer dollar as US yields fell after in-line PCE and the AI selloff.
gbpusd.outlook: Range 1.3280–1.3450, now mid-range; I buy dips near the bottom while BoE hike pricing holds. A close above 1.3450 turns me bullish; below 1.3280 bearish.
gbpusd.watch: The BoE (Nov 5), UK data and US payrolls.

view.call: 1.3280–1.3450; buy dips, BoE Nov 5 is the swing.

audusd.note: Down about 0.35% to 0.7030 after failing at a 0.7068 monthly high near the 50/200-day averages.
audusd.why: Risk sentiment did the moving. The Aussie hit a monthly high of 0.7068 in Asia on hot CPI and Governor Bullock calling inflation far too high, then fell as Alphabet's record plunge hit tech stocks and strong US GDP briefly firmed the dollar. RBA hike odds for Nov 3 stayed high, near 85–88%.
audusd.outlook: My long from 0.7020–0.7035 filled and is flat; I hold for 0.7130 because an RBA hike to 4.85% widens the rate gap. A close below 0.6970, likely on an RBA hold or deeper equity selloff, ends the call.
audusd.watch: China PMIs (Oct 31), the RBA (Nov 3) and US tech stocks.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.1% to 157.71 after a high near 158.1; the BoJ decides Friday.
usdjpy.why: The dollar side slipped. US 10-year yields fell about 8bp as the AI selloff drove buying of Treasuries, outweighing in-line PCE and a 3.4% GDP beat. The yen held firm ahead of a BoJ meeting widely expected to hold at 1.25% while signalling a hike as soon as December.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the short from 157.50–157.80 for 155.00: falling US yields, a hawkish BoJ outlook and Tokyo's guard near 159–160 cap the pair. A close above 158.60, likely on a dovish Ueda, ends the call.
usdjpy.watch: The BoJ and Ueda's briefing (Oct 30), Tokyo CPI and US yields.

view.call: Short from 157.50–157.80; BoJ signals Dec, Tokyo warns.

usdchf.note: Down about 0.45% to 0.8244, near the bottom of its range, as havens rallied.
usdchf.why: The franc did most of the moving. Alphabet's record 12% fall and slumps in ServiceNow and Fortinet sent the Nasdaq down 1.38% and money into havens, while US yields fell. The dollar's failure near 0.8300 earlier this week left room for the drop.
usdchf.outlook: Range 0.8200–0.8300, lowered a notch. A close below 0.8200, the Oct 22 low, would open 0.8150; calm in tech stocks would pull it back toward 0.8300.
usdchf.watch: Swiss CPI (early Nov), US tech earnings and risk sentiment.

usdcad.note: Flat at 1.3989, its lowest 5pm close since Sept 18.
usdcad.why: Two forces cancelled out. Strong US GDP and sticky PCE briefly lifted the pair, but lower US yields and the Bank of Canada's fresh hike to 2.50% kept the loonie firm. It has gained on nine of the past eleven days.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the short from 1.4030–1.4050, about 0.4% in favour, for 1.3850: the BoC–Fed rate gap keeps narrowing. A close above 1.4080, likely on US tariff news, ends the call.
usdcad.watch: Canada GDP (Oct 30), US tariff headlines, oil and payrolls.

view.call: Short from 1.4030–1.4050; BoC hikes, Fed holds.

usdcnh.note: Down about 0.07% to 6.6571; onshore yuan hit 6.6620, strongest since June 2022.
usdcnh.why: The yuan kept grinding up, but the PBOC slowed it. It set the midpoint at 6.7147, its strongest since February 2023 yet 551 pips weaker than the 6.6596 estimate, the widest weak-side gap since Sept. 15. That signals Beijing accepts a firmer yuan but wants a controlled pace.
usdcnh.outlook: Managed grind lower: I sell 6.658–6.665, a lower zone after missing the last one, for 6.620. A close above 6.685 or a China stock selloff ends the call.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China PMIs (Oct 31) and US–China headlines.

view.call: Sell 6.658–6.665; PBOC allows a slow grind up.

usdhkd.note: Flat at 7.8458, still near the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Rate gaps keep it there. Hong Kong interbank rates sit well below US rates, so borrowing Hong Kong dollars to hold US dollars still pays. The pair stayed just short of 7.85, so the HKMA had no need to buy.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in the 7.83–7.85 band. A test of 7.85 would force HKMA buying and lift HIBOR; lower US rates would pull it off the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: HIBOR, HKMA action at 7.85 and US yields.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Down about 0.13% to 1.2799 after failing at 1.2837; S$NEER about 1.5% above mid.
usdsgd.why: The broad dollar did the moving. The pair spiked to 1.2837 after the Fed, then slipped as US yields fell and the yuan touched a three-year high. The Singapore dollar's trade-weighted index sits about 1.5% above the middle of the MAS band, which keeps moves small.
usdsgd.outlook: Range 1.2720–1.2830. A close above 1.2835 would open 1.2855–1.2900; below 1.2720 reopens downside.
usdsgd.watch: The yuan, Singapore data and US payrolls.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 0.9 to 1,336.8 at the Seoul close after a 1,331.3 low; Kospi fell 1.24%.
usdkrw.why: Flows reversed. Foreigners, who bought the most dollar futures this year on Wednesday, turned net sellers after the Fed, pushing the pair from a 1,342 open to 1,331.3. Gains faded as Samsung's results disappointed on shareholder returns and the Kospi fell 1.24% to 5,937.66.
usdkrw.outlook: My sell from 1,335–1,342 filled and is roughly flat; I hold for 1,320 as exporters sell dollars into year-end. A close above 1,345 ends the call.
usdkrw.watch: Korea's October exports (Nov 1), foreign equity flows and US tech stocks.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 7.4 cents to 32.492 after a 32.595 low, as foreigners sold NT$68.8bn of shares.
usdtwd.why: Taiwan's equity flows did the moving. The Taiex fell 1.42% to 46,368 as Alphabet's cash burn revived AI-spending fears, and foreigners turned from buyers to sellers of about NT$68.8 billion. The central bank stepped in late to pull the pair back below 32.50, limiting the day's loss to under 0.25%.
usdtwd.outlook: My fade from 32.53 is slightly in favour after surviving a test of 32.60; I hold for 32.05 because the central bank is leaning hard against weakness. A close above 32.65 on further foreign selling ends the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, Amazon and Intel results, central bank action near 32.50–32.60.

view.call: Fade from 32.53; central bank caps, flows swing.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit rose to 4.0575/0620 at the 6pm close from 4.0745/0790, a third daily gain.
usdmyr.why: Local confidence and a softer dollar did the moving. The ringgit opened firmer on talk that Bank Negara could start normalising its 2.75% policy rate next week, then gained further as the dollar eased after the Fed. As an oil exporter, Malaysia holds up better than its neighbours when Brent sits near $115.
usdmyr.outlook: The break below 4.06 turns my range into a short: I sell 4.065–4.075 for 4.020. A close above 4.095, likely if Bank Negara sounds dovish on Nov 5, ends the call.
usdmyr.watch: Bank Negara (Nov 5), oil and the yuan.

usdphp.note: Peso rose 17.5 centavos to 63.85, a second gain, after trading 63.80–63.91.
usdphp.why: A softer dollar, lower oil in Asian hours and official resolve helped. Traders called the Fed's hold dovish, and President Marcos vowed to use all means to defend the peso after it hit a record 64.18. Volume fell to about $1.46 billion, pointing to short covering rather than fresh inflows.
usdphp.outlook: I book the long from 63.50, about 0.55% up, and move to a 63.50–64.20 range: Manila's pledge and BSP's 5.50% rate cap the topside for now. A close above 64.20 would restart the uptrend; oil and the external gap still limit peso gains.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments, oil and Iran, US midterms (Nov 3).

usdidr.note: Rupiah firmed 47 points to 18,137 (Bloomberg); JISDOR 18,128 from 18,183.
usdidr.why: The dollar side moved. The rupiah rebounded with most of Asia after the Fed's hold, but gains stayed small as foreign investors kept selling Jakarta stocks and risk appetite faded. Bank Indonesia's steady presence near records also limited swings.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long from near 18,000, about 0.75% in favour, for 18,300: outflows over MSCI's review and $115 oil keep pressure on. A close below 18,110 on heavy BI action or an MSCI fix ends the call.
usdidr.watch: MSCI's review, Jakarta flows, BI action and oil.

usdinr.note: Rupee firmed 3 paise to 95.25 (provisional) after a two-week low of 95.38.
usdinr.why: Oil and stocks offset dollar demand. Importer buying pushed the rupee to a two-week low early, but slightly softer crude, hopes for US–Iran talks and firmer Indian stocks pulled it back. Likely RBI dollar sales kept moves narrow.
usdinr.outlook: Range 94.50–95.50: the RBI defends the top while oil above $110 blocks a big rally. A close above 95.50 would signal a new weaker leg.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran, RBI action and foreign flows.

view.call: 94.50–95.50; RBI near the top, oil caps the rupee.

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.15% to near 176.3 as the euro rebounded after the ECB.
eurjpy.why: The euro was the moving leg. It rallied after the ECB kept a December hike on the table while USD/JPY slipped only 0.1%, so the cross rose to about 176.3 (EUR/USD 1.1180 × USD/JPY 157.71).
eurjpy.outlook: My short from 175.90–176.30 is about 0.1% against; I hold for 174.00 into Friday's BoJ. A close above 177.00, likely on a dovish BoJ, ends the call.
eurjpy.watch: The BoJ (Oct 30), euro-area CPI (Oct 30) and risk sentiment.

cnhjpy.note: Little changed near 23.69 as yuan and yen both firmed slightly.
cnhjpy.why: The legs offset. USD/CNH fell about 0.07% and USD/JPY about 0.1%, leaving the cross near 23.69 (USD/JPY 157.71 ÷ USD/CNH 6.6571), in the upper half of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range. A hawkish BoJ would push it toward 23.3; a break above 23.8 would need USD/JPY near 158.6.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, the BoJ on Oct 30 and risk sentiment.

watch: Next: the BoJ, euro-area CPI and Canada GDP (Oct 30), China PMIs (Oct 31), Korea exports (Nov 1), the RBA and US midterms (Nov 3), the BoE and Bank Negara (Nov 5), plus oil, US tech earnings and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
sources: Reuters via Euronext (euro after the ECB)
